item.text:
**Bottom Line**
I found no strong 2024 evidence that Tshisekedi personally incited ethnic, religious, racial, caste, or migrant hatred. The record is instead mostly de-escalatory or sovereignty-focused. The main negative evidence is narrower: he repeatedly scapegoated Rwanda/M23 as aggressors, used war/threat rhetoric, and his government framed dissenters as “enemies,” which helped justify repression. That is concerning, but it is not the same as direct mass-incitement speech.

**Accepted Claims**
- **DRC: President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis** | **Amnesty International** | **2024-06-24** | [source](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/)  
  Amnesty says Tshisekedi’s administration had made little progress on human rights and that conflict and civic-space restrictions persisted. This is background only, but it supports the broader environment in which hostile political framing mattered.  
  **IDs:** `3B.3`, `3B.2`

- **Crackdown framed as defense against enemies** | **Amnesty International** | **2024-09-30** | [source](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/)  
  Amnesty says journalists, civil society activists, and political opponents faced threats, arbitrary detention, and judicial harassment under a crackdown justified as defending the country against enemies. This is indirect evidence of scapegoating opponents and enabling hostility, though not a direct quote of personal hate speech.  
  **IDs:** `3B.3`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`

- **Le Président Felix Tshisekedi réclame des sanctions ciblées contre le Rwanda pour mettre fin à la crise sécuritaire à l’Est de la Rdc** | **Présidence RDC** | **2024-09-25** | [source](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_president_felix_tshisekedi_reclame_des_sanctions_ciblees_contre_le_rwanda_pour_mettre_fin_a_la_crise_securitaire_a_lest_de_la_rdc)  
  Tshisekedi publicly labeled Rwanda an aggressor and M23 a terrorist group and called for targeted sanctions. This is strong external scapegoating and conflict-hardening rhetoric, but the remedy sought was lawful international pressure rather than violence against a domestic group.  
  **IDs:** `3B.3`, `2B.6`, `2B.10`

- **Les Présidents Félix Tshisekedi et Emmanuel Macron ensemble pour le développement et la paix en Rdc** | **Présidence RDC** | **2024-04-30** | [source](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/les_presidents_felix_tshisekedi_et_emmanuel_macron_ensemble_pour_le_developpement_et_la_paix_en_rdc)  
  Tshisekedi framed the eastern crisis around peace, de-escalation, and international support, saying there was “a glimmer of hope” after discussions with Macron. This is counterevidence to a claim that he was personally pushing hatred or revenge.  
  **IDs:** `3B.3`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`

- **UN Secretary-General readout: Tshisekedi discussed eastern DRC and ongoing regional peace efforts** | **United Nations** | **2024-09-24** | [source](https://www.un.org/sg/en/content/sg/readouts/2024-09-24/readout-of-the-secretary-generals-meeting-he-mr-felix-antoine-tshisekedi-tshilombo-president-of-the-democratic-republic-of-the-congo-scroll-down-for-french)  
  The UN readout shows Tshisekedi kept the issue in a diplomatic, peace-process frame rather than an ethnic or sectarian hate frame. This is the clearest positive evidence I found.  
  **IDs:** `3B.3`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`

- **Tshisekedi calls for urgent relaunch of the Nairobi and Luanda peace processes** | **Présidence RDC** | **2024-03-25** | [source](https://presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/crise_securitaire_dans_lest_de_la_rdc_les_presidents_felix_tshisekedi_et_salva_kiir_appellent_au_respect_des_accords_de_paix)  
  Tshisekedi publicly called for peace-process renewal and said he would spare no effort to restore peace, security, and stability. This cuts against a finding of personal incitement.  
  **IDs:** `3B.3`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`

- **Threat rhetoric toward Rwanda** | **Reuters** | **2024-07-04** | [source](https://d2233.cms.socastsrm.com/2024/07/04/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say/)  
  Reuters reported that Tshisekedi threatened to declare war against Rwanda while also relying on proxy forces. This is the strongest direct negative evidence I found for escalation rhetoric, but it is state-directed conflict rhetoric rather than personal incitement against an internal ethnic, religious, or social group.  
  **IDs:** `3B.3`, `2B.6`, `2B.8`

**Search Gap**
I did not find credible 2024 evidence of Tshisekedi personally urging hatred, revenge, dehumanization, or violence against ethnic/religious groups, migrants, journalists, or civil society in the direct sense this lens asks about. What I did find is narrower: external scapegoating of Rwanda/M23, war-threat rhetoric, and an environment where repression of opponents was justified through enemy-framing.
